Pyramid of energy: only 10% moves up
The carbon cycle: one dot, round and round

assessmentPoints: Food-chain arrow answers in the opening activity
Food-web answers in the second activity
Pyramid answers in the third activity
successCriteria: Food chains: arrows follow energy flow: a chain runs producer to primary consumer to secondary consumer, and arrows point from food to feeder, the way energy moves.
Food webs: one dot splits into two: one producer can feed several consumers and one consumer can have several foods, so energy splits across interlinked pathways.
Pyramid of energy: only 10% moves up: most energy is lost as heat and waste, so each level keeps only a tenth and food chains stay short.
objectives.text: Describe energy flow through food chains, food webs and pyramids of energy

assessmentPoints: Carbon-cycle answers in the fourth activity
Conservation answers in the fifth activity
Energy-recycling answers in the closing activity
successCriteria: The carbon cycle: one dot, round and round: photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants, respiration and combustion return it to the air, and decomposers release carbon from dead matter.
Conservation: when habitat shrinks, species vanish: fragmentation isolates small populations, and protected corridors reconnect fragments so species can move again.
A common mistake: energy is not recycled: energy flows one way and leaves as heat, while matter such as carbon is what actually cycles.
objectives.text: Explain the carbon cycle, conservation and why energy is not recycled
